the study of the chiral phase transitions of the three flavor quark matter at finite temperature and chemical potential.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the restoration of the full chiral symmetry occurs in a two-step process, where the axial symmetry is the first one to be restored.
the axial part is restored first and then, as temperature and density increase, the full chiral symmetry is also restored.
the restoration of chrial SU$(3)\times$SU$(3)\times$I and axial U$_{A}(1)$ symmetries occurs at a temperature and density that is not too far from the one at which the quark condensate vanishes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the restoration of U(1)$_A$ is the main mechanism responsible for the restoration of chrial symmetry at finite temperature and/or density.
the restoration of the chiral symmetry is driven mainly by the temperature dependence of the anomaly.
the U$_A$(0) symmetry is restored before U$_A$(3) symmetry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the axial symmetry is restored at lower temperatures (densities) than the chiral symmetry.
the restoration of the axial part of U$_A$ symmetry, which is a consequence of the anomaly, is an essential ingredient for the restoration of the chiral SU(3)\otimes SU$(3)$ symmetry.
